Fetch an Esri Wayback release as a local raster around an AOI

Source: R/dft_wayback_fetch.R
dft_wayback_fetch.Rd

Reads one Wayback release's tiles at one zoom over aoi and returns a three-band (red, green, blue) 8-bit raster, cached as a COG. Take the release_id and zoom from dft_wayback_pick(), so the raster shows the capture you chose.

Usage

dft_wayback_fetch(
  aoi,
  release,
  zoom,
  crs = NULL,
  res = NULL,
  clip = TRUE,
  empty_max = 0.05,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  force = FALSE
)

Arguments

aoi

An sf, sfc or terra::SpatVector of polygons. Several features are fetched as their union.

release

A Wayback release_id (from dft_wayback_releases() or dft_wayback_pick()).

zoom

One tile zoom level in 10 to 22, normally the zoom that dft_wayback_pick() returns with the release.

crs

Output CRS (e.g. "EPSG:3005"). When NULL, the UTM zone of the AOI centroid.

res

Output cell size in CRS units. When NULL, the tiles' own ground resolution at the AOI's latitude (Web Mercator pixels shrink by the cosine of the latitude), rounded to 0.05 m: zoom 17 is 0.70 m at 54 degrees north. Required for a geographic crs.

clip

Logical. Set cells whose centre is outside aoi to nodata (default TRUE). FALSE keeps the whole bounding box.

empty_max

Numeric in 0 to 1. The largest share of the AOI's cells that may come back empty before the call aborts (default 0.05).

cache_dir

Character. Cache directory. When NULL, uses dft_cache_path().

force

Logical. Re-build the raster even if cached (default FALSE).

Value

A terra::SpatRaster with layers red, green, blue (INT1U, nodata 0), backed by the cached COG.

Details

GDAL reads the tiles. It follows the redirect a release answers with for a tile it shares with an older release, which QGIS does not (qgis/QGIS#54161), so a cached local raster is also the way to draw a Wayback capture in QGIS. Tiles are always read at zoom itself, never from a shallower level GDAL would otherwise substitute for a coarse res, since a shallower level can show another capture.

The finished raster is cached; the tiles are not. GDAL's own tile cache turns every missing (404) tile into a pair of read errors (measured on GDAL 3.13.0), and a fetch that treats GDAL errors as failures cannot tell those from a real one. A cache hit downloads nothing; a new grid re-downloads.

Empty tiles. A tile the release does not have (HTTP 404) reads as zeros. A pixel that is zero in all three bands is treated as empty and becomes nodata, and the call aborts (class drift_wayback_empty) when more than empty_max of the AOI is empty: the release has no imagery at that zoom there. A FLAT area is not empty: open water is flat. Elsewhere a band value of 0 is raised to 1, because 0 is the nodata value.

Per point, one call each. For chips around sample points, buffer each point and call once per buffered point, as for dft_stac_composite(); each chip is cached separately. Points themselves are refused. With clip = TRUE a cell belongs to the AOI when its centre does, so AOIs that tile the ground without overlap, such as Voronoi cells around the points, produce chips that share no cell. A VRT over such chips then shows each point's own capture at the point: it composites over nodata, which is why these are nodata-masked and not alpha-masked.

Mosaics need one grid. The default crs is the UTM zone of the AOI and the default res follows its latitude, so chips spread over a large area can differ in both. Pass the same crs and res to every call whose outputs will be mosaicked.

A polygon's fetch shows whatever the release draws there, which can be several captures (see cover in dft_wayback_captures()).

See also

dft_wayback_captures(), dft_wayback_pick(), dft_map_interactive() (rgb =) to display it.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aoi <- sf::st_read(system.file("extdata", "example_aoi.gpkg", package = "drift"))
pts <- sf::st_as_sf(sf::st_sample(aoi, 5, type = "regular"))
cap <- dft_wayback_captures(pts)
pick <- dft_wayback_pick(cap, as.Date("2017-07-01"))

# One chip per point, +/-150 m, on one grid so they can be mosaicked
buf <- sf::st_buffer(pts, 150, endCapStyle = "SQUARE")
chips <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pick)), function(i) {
  dft_wayback_fetch(buf[pick$feature[i], ], pick$release_id[i], pick$zoom[i],
                    crs = "EPSG:3005", res = 0.7)
})
terra::plotRGB(chips[[1]])
} # }
